    Pre-foreclosures — call the owners who still have equity
    Nobody is selling these yet. Value is Zillow's estimate; Owed is only the loan being foreclosed, when Zillow shows it. Equity = value − owed. Run Liens0101 and the docket before you call.
    Short sales — asking price vs your max offer
    Resale value comes from closed comps (Zillow's estimate on a short sale just copies the asking price). Max offer = resale × 0.90 − rehab − the larger of 15% of resale or $25K.

    Floor List — clean first-lien houses you can buy at the plaintiff's floor, with the exact bid

    BID = bid this number (floor + $100 when the clerk shows the plaintiff's max; otherwise proxy up to your max — the bank cannot ask more than the judgment). WATCH = floor hidden and the judgment is above your max: bid only if the plaintiff opens under it. Net is after rehab, closing, carry, 6% selling costs and any surviving senior debt. Title search before any bid.

    Read before bidding: Grades rate screening attractiveness, not purchase price — plaintiffs credit-bid to their judgment and competition pushes clean deals toward 70–85% of value. Set max bid = 70% of verified value − rehab − $15K friction, and never exceed it. How the grade is set: circuit-court mortgage cases with judgment ≤35% of appraiser value grade A, ≤45% A-, ≤52% B+, ≤60% B; 60–70% is C+ (only works below judgment) and above 70% is D. Judgments under 18% of value (or under $50K) are treated as likely junior-lien/HOA sales and capped at C, under 6% as bait (D); county-court cases are D because the first mortgage survives; tax deeds are capped at B because the opening bid is only the tax debt. Miami-Dade houses take a one-notch penalty (clean SFHs there hammer at ~100% of value) and sales inside 5 days take one more. Duval (Jacksonville) is graded on the same ladder; its benchmarks come from its own auction results. Rehab is estimated at $45/sf of living area. Amber/red rows with tiny judgments are likely junior-lien/HOA sales where senior debt survives. Title search mandatory before any bid — IRS, code-enforcement, and municipal liens are invisible here. Sources: miamidade / broward / palmbeach / duval / hillsborough / pinellas / charlotte .realforeclose.com · county Property Appraisers · US Census geocoder · FEMA. Not financial or legal advice.
